37 A battery with negligible internal resistance is connected to three resistors, as shown.
0.30 A
X
All three resistors have the same resistance.
The current in the battery is 0.30 A.
What is the current in resistor X?
A
0.10 A
B
0.15 A
C
0.20 A
D
0.30 A

hints: Notice from the diagram that resistor X forms one parallel branch while the other two equal resistors in series form the second parallel branch.
Recall that parallel branches have the same potential difference, so branch current is $I = V/R$ and is larger where branch resistance is smaller.
Compare the resistance $R$ of the X-branch with the $2R$ resistance of the lower branch to find the current ratio, then share the $0.30\text{ A}$ total in that ratio.
walkthrough: Identify the two parallel branches between the dots: the upper branch is resistor X with resistance $R$, and the lower branch is two resistors in series with total resistance $R+R = 2R$.
State the rule for parallel circuits: both branches have the same potential difference $V$, so $I_X = V/R$ and $I_{lower} = V/(2R)$.
Divide the expressions to get the ratio: $I_X/I_{lower} = 2R/R = 2$, so the current in X is twice the current in the lower branch.
Apply Kirchhoff's current law at the junction: $I_X + I_{lower} = 0.30\text{ A}$, so $2I_{lower} + I_{lower} = 0.30\text{ A}$.
Solve: $3I_{lower} = 0.30\text{ A}$ gives $I_{lower} = 0.10\text{ A}$, so $I_X = 0.20\text{ A}$. This is option C.

A.explanation: This would be the current in the lower branch, not in X. The $2R$ branch takes one third of the total $0.30\text{ A}$.

B.explanation: This assumes the $0.30\text{ A}$ splits equally. The branches do not have equal resistance, so the currents are not equal.

C.explanation: X has resistance $R$ in parallel with $2R$, so it carries twice the current of the lower branch, which is two thirds of $0.30\text{ A}$.

D.explanation: This is the total battery current. Only part of it goes through X because the current divides at the junction.
